newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures end lower, pound skids.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures end lower, pound skids.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended moderately lower Thursday, while sterling skidded to hefty losses that erased Tuesday's equally large gains.
Afternoon trade slowed from an active morning as futures mirrored swings in U.S. asset markets and erased the bulk of early morning losses when U.S. Treasury bond and stock index markets slumped.

T-bonds slid, tugging stock index products down to sharp losses, as players fretted that the economy might be picking up enough steam to make inflation a concern and prod the Federal Reserve into raising interest rates.

T-bond futures initially firmed after weekly U.S. jobless claims rose more than expected. But they switched course and tumbled to a loss of more than a point after National Purchasing Managers association said its December index rose to 54.0 against forecasts for 51.5.
Components of that index, including prices, rose and made traders increasingly jittery about the inflation outlook.

Late in the session, Canadian dollar also broke down to the day's low, with one fund selling about 1,000 March futures starting at $0.7312 to the low. A fund, possibly the same, also sold some 1,000 March sterling on the day, brokers said.
Sterling skidded on what brokers said was a technical correction of its recent rally to contract highs.
"It looked like a correction from the (rally in) thin markets this week," said a broker of sterling. "I'm still dollar- and pound-bullish. I still like the dollar and cable."
Thursday's selloff, however, pushed it below important supports and made at least some brokers think the contract still could correct further before heading back up again.
"Sterling has broken through some pretty significant support," said another broker. "We've broken through 1.6874 and have some more downside."

At settlement, March yen rose $0.000029 to $0.008742, marks eased $0.0009 to $0.6522, Swiss francs lost $0.0032 to $0.7488, sterling skidded $0.0222 to $1.6902, Canadian dollar lost $0.0034 to $0.7298, Aussie dollar lost $0.0035 to $0.7901, and Mexican peso rose $0.000100 to $0.121450.
